CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate treatment response for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, with a focus on symptom improvement and medication tolerability since the last appointment.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith presents for his follow-up visit, reporting notable changes in his symptomatology since his last appointment. He expresses a significant reduction in anxiety-related symptoms, with fewer episodes of irritability and improved coping mechanisms during high-stress situations, which he attributes to continued cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) sessions. He remains compliant with sertraline at 300 mg daily, and while he acknowledges some cognitive challenges persist, he describes them as less disruptive than previously experienced.
Mr. Smith reports a decrease in the frequency of tension-type headaches, now occurring once weekly, with intensity averaging 3 to 5 out of 10. He has been diligent in maintaining a headache diary, which indicates a correlation between headache occurrences and high-stress days at work. He continues to use topiramate at 150 mg daily, and although he still occasionally resorts to ibuprofen, he states that he has reduced its use to approximately twice a month.
Sleep quality has improved, with Mr. Smith averaging 7 to 9 hours of sleep nightly, aided by trazodone and melatonin. He reports diminished morning grogginess, which he attributes to better sleep hygiene practices and a consistent bedtime routine. Mr. Smith has also incorporated light stretching exercises into his daily regimen, which he believes have positively affected his overall well-being and energy levels.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 300 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (decreased use) 5. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 6. Topiramate 150 mg daily (continued) 7. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 8. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime (continued) 9. Modafinil 100 mg in the morning (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to engage in regular physical activity, including brisk walking and yoga, which he finds beneficial for managing his anxiety and enhancing his mood. He maintains a balanced diet and has further reduced his caffeine intake, which he believes has contributed to his improved sleep quality. His mindfulness practices remain integral to his routine, and he reports that he has been more consistent in his meditation practices, which he finds helpful in managing stress.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Significant improvement in anxiety; cognitive difficulties persist but are less disruptive; sleep quality improved; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Decreased headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Fatigue is well-managed, particularly with modafinil; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/76 mmHg, HR 68 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented; appears well-rested and engaged; mood appears stable with mild anxiety. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no tenderness in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with mild anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 300 mg daily. Reinforce the importance of ongoing CBT to address residual cognitive concerns. Reassess in one month for potential dose adjustments if symptoms plateau. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 75 mg at bedtime and melatonin 3 mg nightly; reassess in one month for efficacy and side effects. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 150 mg daily; maintain headache diary to monitor frequency and intensity. If the trend does not improve, consider referral to a neurologist for further evaluation. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue modafinil at 100 mg in the morning; monitor for efficacy. Encourage continued stress management techniques and regular physical activity.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-09-19 to evaluate symptom progression, medication effectiveness, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is encouraged to maintain open communication regarding his treatment response and any lifestyle changes he implements.
